Requirement: A SpaceWire Port shall incorporate a transmit FIFO (TX FIFO) which stores N-Chars provided by the application via the SpaceWire port interface until they can be sent across the link.
A SpaceWire Port shall incorporate a receive FIFO (RX FIFO) which stores received N-Chars until they can be read by the application via the SpaceWire port interface.
Null is passed to the encoding layer by the data link layer whenever a link is not sending data or control symbols, to keep the link active and to support link disconnect detection.

When the SpaceWire output port is reset, it shall be a controlled reset avoiding simultaneous transitions of Data and Strobe signals. For example, after stopping transmission the Strobe signal can be reset first, followed by the Data signal. This prevents a simultaneous transition on the data and strobe signals which can cause some IEEE 1355-1995 devices to enter an unrecoverable fault state
Response: G((output_port_reset & transmition_stopped) -> ((!data_transition U reset_strobe_signal) & (reset_strobe_signal -> X(!Strobe_signal_transition U reset_data_signal))))

Requirement: gotNull shall be asserted when the first Null after the receiver is enabled is detected
The disconnect detection shall be enabled when the link state machine leaves the ErrorReset state and the first edge is detected on the Data or Strobe line

An escape character (ESC) followed by ESC, EOP or EEP is an invalid sequence and when received shall produce an ESC error. ESC followed by FCT is a Null and ESC followed by a data character is a broadcast code
Ground Truth: G( (((ESC_received & X ESC_received) | (ESC_received & X EOP_received)) | (ESC_received & X EEP_received )) -> (ESC_error) ) & G( (ESC_received & X FCT_received) -> Null) & G((ESC_received & X data_received) -> (broadcast_code) )
Atomic Proposition: {CT_received, EEP_received, EOP_received, ESC_error, ESC_received, Null, broadcast_code, data_received}
Response: G((ESC_received & X(ESC_received | EOP_received | EEP_received)) -> X(ESC_error)) & G((ESC_received & X(Null)) -> X(Null)) & G((ESC_received & X(data_received)) -> X(broadcast_code))

Requirement: The data link layer shall not send any N-Chars to the encoding layer until it has received one or more FCTs from the encoding layer to indicate that the data link layer at the other end of the link is ready to receive N-Chars
Parity Error, ESC Error, gotFCT, gotN-Char and gotBC are only enabled after the first Null has been received (i.e. gotNull asserted)
Disconnect Error is only enabled after the first transition on the data or strobe line
When Port Reset is asserted, the following actions shall occur: 1.The TX FIFO and RX FIFO are cleared 2.The link state machine enters the ErrorReset state

The Link state machine shall leave the Run state on one of the following conditions: 1.When LinkDisabled is asserted, move to the ErrorReset state. 2.When a disconnect occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 3.When a parity error occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 4.When an ESC error occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 5.When a credit error occurs, move to the ErrorReset state
Ground Truth: G ( ( ((((LinkDisabled | disconnect) | parity_error) | ESC_error) | credit_error) ) -> X (ErrorReset_state) )
Response: G((LinkDisabled | disconnect | parity_error | ESC_error | credit_error) -> X(ErrorReset_state))

Requirement: When the link state machine is in the Run state and sending of a broadcast code is requested, it shall be sent as soon as the data link layer has finished sending the current character or control code
When sending of an FCT is requested, it shall be sent as soon as the current character or control code has been sent provided that: No broadcast code is waiting to be sent
When LinkDisabled is asserted in the Ready state, the link state machine remains in the Ready state
When LinkDisabled is asserted in the Run state, the link state machine moves to the ErrorReset state

The Link state machine shall leave the Ready state on one of the following conditions: 1.When LinkDisabled is asserted, move to the ErrorReset state. 2.When a disconnect occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 3.When a parity error occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 4.When an ESC error occurs, move to the ErrorReset state. 5.When an FCT, N-Char or broadcast code is received from the Encoding Layer, move to the ErrorReset state. 6.When LinkStart is asserted, move to the Started state. 7.When AutoStart is asserted and gotNull is asserted, move to the Started state
Ground Truth: G((LinkDisabled) -> X (ErrorReset)) & G((disconnect) -> X (ErrorReset)) & G((parity) -> X (ErrorReset)) & G((ESC_Error) -> (ErrorReset)) & G(((FCT_received) | (NChar_received) | (broadcast_received)) -> X(ErrorReset)) & G((LinkStart_asserted) -> X(Started_state)) & G(((AutoStart_asserted) | (gotNull_asserted)) -> X(Started_state))
Atomic Proposition: {AutoStart_asserted, CT_received, ESC_Error, ErrorReset, LinkDisabled, LinkStart_asserted, NChar_received, Started_state, broadcast_received, disconnect, gotNull_asserted, parity}
Response: G(((LinkDisabled | disconnect | parity | ESC_Error | NChar_received | broadcast_received) -> X(ErrorReset)) & ((LinkStart_asserted | (AutoStart_asserted & gotNull_asserted)) -> X(Started_state)))

Requirement: This alternative behaviour allows the link state machine of the previous version of the SpaceWire standard ECSS-E-ST-50-12C (31 July 2008) to be used. The improvement in the current version (Revision 1) means that the link state machine immediately moves to and remains in the ErrorReset state with the receiver disabled, when Disable is asserted. The functions of Disable/Enable, Link Start and Autostart have been separated for clarity
When Port Reset is asserted, the Link Error Recovery state machine shall enter the Normal state

The Link Error Recovery state machine shall leave the Normal state on the following conditions: 1.When the Link state machine is in the Run state and LinkDisabled is asserted, the Link Error Recovery state machine moves to the Recovery state. 2.When the Link state machine is in the Run state and a Disconnect, Parity Error, ESC Error, or Credit Error occurs, the Link Error Recovery state machine moves to the Recovery state
Atomic Proposition: {Credit_Error, Disconnect, ESC_Error, LinkDisabled_asserted, Parity_Error, Recovery_state, Run_State, Run_state}
Response: G(((Run_state & LinkDisabled_asserted) | (Run_state & (Disconnect | Parity_Error | ESC_Error | Credit_Error))) -> X(Recovery_state))

Requirement: When in the Recovery state, the Link Error Recovery state machine shall initiate the following actions: 1.If currently sending a packet, discard the remainder of the packet that has not yet been sent. 2.If the last character written to the receive FIFO was a data character, write an EEP to the receive FIFO. 3.When the last character written was an EOP or EEP, another EEP can be added to the receive FIFO. 4.If an EEP is pending, ready for writing to the receive FIFO and that FIFO is full preventing an EEP being written, wait until there is space in the receive FIFO and then write the EEP. 5.Record the cause of the error in a status register
Ground Truth: G((Recovery_state) -> (((sending_current_packet) & (a_packet_not_sent)) -> X(discard_remainder))) & (G((Recovery_state) -> ((last_character_is_data) -> X(EEP_sent_to_receive_FIFO))) & (G((Recovery_state) -> ((last_character_EOP | last_character_EEP) -> X(EEP_sent_to_receive_FIFO))) & (G((Recovery_state) -> ( (((EEP_pending) & (FIFO_full)) -> ((EEP_wait) U (EEP_in_receive_FIFO))) -> X(write_EEP))) & G((Recovery_state) -> ((error) -> X (Record_error))))))
Atomic Proposition: {EEP_in_receive_FIFO, EEP_pending, EEP_sent_to_receive_FIFO, EEP_wait, IFO_full, Record_error, Recovery_state, a_packet_not_sent, discard_remainder, error, last_character_EEP, last_character_EOP, last_character_is_data, sending_current_packet, write_EEP}
Response: G((Recovery_state & sending_current_packet) -> discard_remainder) & G((Recovery_state & last_character_is_data) -> write_EEP) & G((Recovery_state & (last_character_EOP | last_character_EEP)) -> EEP_sent_to_receive_FIFO) & G((Recovery_state & EEP_pending & IFO_full) -> (EEP_wait U (!IFO_full & write_EEP))) & G(Recovery_state -> Record_error)

Requirement: If one or more N-Chars have been sent since the link reached the Run state AND the last character sent was not an EOP or EEP, read the transmit FIFO and discard the characters read until an EOP or EEP has been read and discarded
Ground Truth: G(  ((Run_state_started) -> ((NChar_sent) & !(last_char_EOP | EEP)))  -> X(((read_transmit_FIFO) & (discard_characters)) U ((EOP_read | EEP_read) & (EOP_discard | EEP_discarded)))  )
Atomic Proposition: {EEP, EEP_discarded, EEP_read, EOP_discard, EOP_read, NChar_sent, Run_state_started, discard_characters, last_char_EOP, read_transmit_FIFO}
Response: G((Run_state_started & NChar_sent & !(last_char_EOP) & !(EEP)) -> (read_transmit_FIFO & discard_characters) U (EOP_read & EOP_discard & EEP_read & EEP_discarded))

Requirement: If the receive FIFO is full it is not possible for the transmitter to send an FCT, hence the link initialisation cannot be completed. The link state machine cycles through the ErrorReset, ErrorWait, Ready and Started state and then times out in the Connecting state because no FCT can be received. When there is room for at least eight N-Chars, at least one FCT can be sent so the link initialisation process is then able to complete successfully.

The Link Error Recovery state machine shall leave the Recovery state on the following conditions: When all error recovery actions, listed in 5.5.8.4.b are successfully completed, move to the Normal state
An output port shall not transmit any other packet until the packet that it is currently transmitting has finished being sent or has been terminated following an error
If the allocated output port is busy, the newly arrived packet shall wait at the input port until the allocated output port is free to transmit the new packet

When the allocated output port becomes free, the input port connected to it after arbitration shall transfer one packet to the output port and then free the output port for subsequent arbitration and use by the same or another input port

If one or more of the output ports in the multicast set cannot accept a new N-Char during packet transfer, the input port waits, and the N-Char is not sent to any of the multicast output ports until they are all ready
On receipt of the DISTRIBUTED-INTERRUPT.request primitive the SpaceWire end-point shall immediately send the interrupt code through its port
On receipt of the BROADCAST-CODE.request primitive the port shall send the broadcast code immediately after the character current has finished being sent
The effect on receipt of the DISCONNECT.indication primitive by the data link layer shall be for data link layer to move to the ErrorReset state
The effect on receipt of the RECEIVE-ERROR.indication primitive by the data link layer shall be for data link layer to move to the ErrorReset state
The function of the gotNull.indication primitive shall be to indicate to the data link layer that the first Null has been received after the receiver has been enabled
The gotNull.indication primitive shall be passed to the data link layer, when the first Null is received without any errors after the receiver has been enabled.
Received characters and control codes shall be passed to the data link layer in the order in which they are received.

If the host system tries to send an interrupt acknowledgement too soon after a corresponding interrupt code has been received, i.e. before the interrupt code has propagated across the entire network, the result is indeterminate for that specific interrupt. The new interrupt acknowledgement code that the node sends can either be discarded by a router, or repeatedly propagated through the network if the network has circular connections.
